thread.title: UPDATE: After GM cuts, Wall Street cheer turns to auto-bubble fear

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: After GM cuts, Wall Street cheer turns to auto-bubble fear
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
While the tech sector has gripped us lately, autos are stealing some limelight after GM announced plant closures and job losses (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gm-stock-skyrockets-after-car-maker-unveils-plan-to-slash-jobs-close-plants-2018-11-26) on Monday.
Shares initially got a boost on the theory that cost cuts boost profits. But the mood could yet turn less positive for the sector as a whole.
That brings us to our call of the day, from Clarity Financial analyst Jesse Colombo, who sees trouble ahead for the auto sector. "Rising interest rates are threatening U.S. automobile sales and loan bubble and will eventually cause its popping," he warned in a blog post (https://realinvestmentadvice.com/gm-cuts-14700-jobs-as-auto-bubble-begins-to-burst/).
"While GM's CEO Mary Barra is spinning this move as a positive, I am highly suspicious because it is taking place at the same time that global auto sales are plunging," explains Colombo, who warned about another bubble-soon-to-burst (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/analyst-who-predicted-the-2008-crash-warns-of-bubble-brewing-in-us-household-wealth-2018-10-18) linked to household wealth and easy Fed policy, in October. Here's his chart:
Colombo delivered a similar warning a year ago when Ford announced investments in Michigan, and he notes that auto maker has also recently announced an $11 billion restructuring.
Since 2010, total outstanding U.S. auto loans are up $445 billion or 64% to over $1.1 trillion as Americans used record low interest rates to finance new cars, adds Colombo. "Low interest rates lead to borrowing booms that end when interest rates go back up, which is what has been happening over the past few years," he warns.
Last word goes to Wolf Richter at the Wolf Street blog, who says GM's plans will cost $3.8 billion, much of which will have to be borrowed. And that is because the auto maker "blew, wasted, and annihilated $13.9 billion in cash on share buybacks over the past four years," he says, providing this chart:
To add insult to injury, GM's shares fell 10% during that four-year period, even if they got a bump on Monday, Richter points out. You can read his full rant here (https://wolfstreet.com/2018/11/26/gm-after-14-bn-share-buybacks-prepares-for-carmageddon-shift-to-evs-cuts-workers-closes-8-plants/).
The market
Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are pulling back. That is after a strong session for the S&P , Dow and Nasdaq as retailers rose on Cyber Monday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/global-stocks-dow-futures-regain-ground-as-oil-prices-rebound-2018-11-26).
Read:Jim Cramer sees signs of a 'classic bear market' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cnbcs-cramer-says-stocks-are-opening-up-huge-on-nothing-sees-signs-of-classic-bear-market-2018-11-26)
Crude is flat, while gold is inching up and the dollar is up as the pound drops on Brexit-deal concerns.
Check out the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/markets) for the latest action.
Europe stocks are struggling, and Asia traded mixed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-cool-off-as-investors-await-trump-xi-meeting-2018-11-26), with investors wary ahead of the Trump/Xi meeting.
Opinion:How to avoid making stupid investing mistakes when the stock market drops (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-to-avoid-making-stupid-investing-mistakes-when-the-stock-market-drops-2018-11-26)
The chart
Société Générale has laid out its outlook for 2019, with this bottom-line advice for investors: diversify out of the dollar. Here it is in a nutshell, making for our chart of the day:
The buzz
Apple (AAPL) is under pressure (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trumps-saber-rattling-ahead-of-china-trade-talks-hurts-apple-2018-11-26) ahead of the open after POTUS said Chinese-made MacBooks and iPhones could be subject to tariffs. It adds to investor agita (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-stock-drops-as-trumps-tariffs-comments-add-to-investor-agita-analyst-says-2018-11-27), says Wedbush analysts. And plans to boost tariffs on China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-says-highly-unlikely-that-china-will-avoid-facing-tariff-hikes-2018-11-26)has also cast some doubt on whether trade talks in Buenos Aires this weekend can go off without a hitch.

Tesla (TSLA) shares are down after the auto maker's China sales reportedly tumbled 70% from a year ago (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/teslas-china-sales-fell-70-in-october-as-trade-conflict-weighed-reuters-2018-11-27).
Read: These stocks are in bear territory, but analysts expect them to roar back (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-stocks-are-in-bear-territory-but-analysts-expect-them-to-roar-back-2018-11-26)
Cyber Monday sales are expected to hit $7.9 billion by Monday's end, the biggest online shopping day of all time. Revenue from smartphones will hit $2.1 billion on Cyber Monday ($1.4 billion in 2017), making it the highest ever at 48.1% growth, says Adobe Analytics.
One of the last big U.S. industrial conglomerates, United Technologies (UTX), plans to break apart into three independent companies (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/united-tech-to-break-into-three-companies-spinning-off-otis-and-carrier-2018-11-26).
The economy
Case-Shiller house prices and consumer confidence are ahead, and we'll hear from a bunch of Fed speakers--Vice Chair Richard Clarida along with Atlanta, Kansas City and Chicago Fed Presidents Raphael Bostic, Esther George and Charles Evans.
Read:Here's why climate change is so bad for the economy (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-what-the-climate-change-report-says-would-happen-to-the-economy-if-temperatures-keep-get-hotter-2018-11-26)
The stat
200 million -- that is the latest tally (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-11-26/fortnite-now-has-200-million-players-up-60-from-the-last-count?cmpid=socialflow-twitter-business&utm_campaign=socialflow-organic&utm_content=business&utm_source=twitter&utm_medium=social) on those playing the wildly popular Fortnite shooting game, which is up 60% from a June update, and five times higher than in January.
Byron Lotter, money manager at Vestact notes that Fortnite owner, Epic Games, raised funds in October, that value the business at $15 billion. "That makes Tencent's stake worth $6bn, bigger than Gowthpoint, Aspen and Woolworths," said Lotter, in a note to clients.. Hong-Kong-based Tencent (0700.HK) owns a 40% stake in the Epic Games.
